newsitem.title: USA: Dollar jumps to top level against mark in over 3 years.
newsitem.headline: Dollar jumps to top level against mark in over 3 years.

text.p: The dollar surged to its highest level against the German mark in over three years on Monday, buoyed by concerns about European monetary union and robust U.S. economic data.
The mark was hit once again by questions about the strength of Europe's planned single currency, known as the euro, which is scheduled for introduction in 1999.

Over the weekend, Germany's central bank president, Hans Tietmeyer, said sustainable budgetary discipline was a more important goal than meeting the strict fiscal guidelines designed to ensure a strong euro.

And on Monday, German Chancellor Helmut Kohl played down a rift with his party's ruling coalition partners over monetary union and said his government was fully united in its drive to launch the single currency on time.

The remarks convinced the market of Germany's resolve to push ahead with the single currency regardless of its ability to meet the economic requirements for its launch, weighing on the mark and pushing the dollar higher.
"The feeling is that we're going to have a broad and weak euro," said Bob Savage, chief foreign exchange dealer at Lehman Brothers.
The dollar rose to a peak of 1.7465 marks Monday, its highest level since February 1994. It ended the day at 1.7455 marks, up from 1.7395 late Friday.
The dollar also benefited from a series of strong U.S. economic reports Monday which suggested that growth could be picking up again after several months of slowing.

New home sales showed robust growth in May, while both Chicago and New York manufacturing indexes posted strong gains for the month of June, suggesting that Tuesday's national manufacturing report from the National Association of Purchasing Management will also show strength.

Economists are not anticipating an interest rate hike from the Federal Reserve following their upcoming two-day meeting Tuesday and Wednesday, but traders said Monday's numbers kept hopes for an August rate rise alive.
Higher interest rates would make yields on U.S. investments more attractive, boosting the dollar.

"We have economic numbers which seem to imply that the second quarter is now waking up," said Hillel Waxman, chief dealer at Bank Leumi Trust Co. of New York. "Nobody expects anything this week from the Fed, but the possibility of an interest rate hike in August is there."
In other action Monday, the mark slumped to its lowest level against the British pound in almost five years.
A strong gain in British consumer credit fuelled chances of an interest rate increase Monday, boosting the pound to its top level against the mark since July 1992.
"There is certainly a lot of life coming out of the UK," said Waxman. "The expectation is that there will be a rate hike."

In other trade on Monday, the dollar rose to 114.68 Japanese yen from 114.61 late on Friday. It pushed up to 1.4615 Swiss francs from 1.4525. The pound closed stronger at $1.6645 against $1.6632. The dollar ended unchanged at Canadian $1.3807.
